recipes.name: Pan de Yema (Oaxacan Egg Bread)
recipes.flavorProfile: Soft, golden and lightly sweet, with cinnamon and vanilla and a sugar crust on top.
recipes.healthBenefit: Whole eggs bring protein and choline; it is an enriched bread made with a good deal of lard and sugar.

ingredients.baseName: Grains, wheat flour, white, bread flour

ingredients.prepNote: 350 g in the dough, about 30 g sprinkled on top
½ cup, 5 tablespoons of it warmed for the yeast
ingredients.baseName: Milk, whole, 3.25% milkfat, with added vitamin D

instructions: Dissolve the yeast in 5 tablespoons of the milk, warmed.

Make a well in the flour and put the sugar, 250 g of lard, the eggs, cinnamon, vanilla and the rest of the milk in the middle. Add the yeast and knead until the dough comes away from the table by itself. Add a little more flour if it is too wet.
Shape into a ball, grease it with a little lard, cover with a cloth and leave in a warm place about 2½ hours, until doubled.
Shape peach-sized balls on a greased tray, brush them with lard and leave 1½ hours more, until doubled.
Flatten them a little with your palm, sprinkle with sugar and bake at 180°C (350°F) for about 30 minutes, until the base sounds hollow when tapped.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the sugar in the dough and sprinkled on top, a large amount per bun.

citations.source: Programa Destinos México: Gastronomía de San Pablo Villa de Mitla

recipes.curationNote: Programa Destinos México, Gastronomía de San Pablo Villa de Mitla (pan de yema) for every amount and step; made at the source size: 1 kg flour, 250 g lard plus 1 tablespoon, 13 eggs, ½ cup milk, 1 sachet yeast, 350 g sugar, 2 tsp cinnamon, 1 tsp vanilla. Peach-sized buns come to about 16. The source uses no salt.

recipes.name: Chiles Güeros en Escabeche
recipes.flavorProfile: Tangy, mildly hot and herby, with carrot and onion in the brine.
recipes.healthBenefit: Peppers and carrot bring vitamin C and carotenes in a pickle with little fat.

ingredients.prepNote: güero chiles; the database has Hungarian wax pepper
the share eaten with the vegetables; the jar holds 500 ml

ingredients.baseName: Onions, spring or scallions (includes tops and bulb)

instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot. Add the onions, carrots and chiles and fry about 6 minutes.
Add the cauliflower, oregano, thyme, salt and pepper and fry 2 minutes more.
Pour in the vinegar and boil about 5 minutes. If it is too sharp, add a little water and bring it back to the boil.
Jar with the oil and liquid, cool and keep in the fridge. One serving is 50 g of vegetables.
recipes.curationNote: México Desconocido, Chiles en escabeche for every amount and step; the source is for 1 kg of jalapeños and makes 2 kg; this is half, with güero chiles in place of the jalapeños. It frys the vegetables in 1 litre of oil for the full batch, and salts and peppers to taste.

recipes.name: Pan Molido (Dry Breadcrumbs)
recipes.healthBenefit: Made from bolillos at home, with nothing added.

components.note: all 10 rolls, a few days old, dried

instructions: Slice the stale bolillos and dry them in a 120 C (250 F) oven for about 1 hour, until crisp.
Cool and grind fine. Keep in a closed jar for a month.

recipes.name: Chocolate de Mesa (Mexican Table Chocolate)
recipes.flavorProfile: Grainy, sweet and cinnamon-scented, made for whisking into hot drinks and mole.
recipes.healthBenefit: Cocoa brings magnesium, iron and flavanols; the sugar is high, so it is used by the piece.

ingredients.prepNote: 700 g cacao beans, roasted, skinned and ground

instructions: Grind the roasted, skinned cacao to a paste in a processor or on a metate.
Add the sugar, cinnamon and melted cocoa butter and keep grinding until smooth.
Press into discs about 8 cm across and rest them 24 hours in the fridge. Each disc of about 30 g makes one cup when whisked into hot milk or water.
recipes.curationNote: elGourmet, Chocolate de metate for every amount and step; made at the source size: 700 g roasted cacao beans, 500 g sugar, 1 tablespoon ground cinnamon, 100 g cocoa butter. Ground cacao is cocoa mass.

recipes.name: Chocolate Oaxaqueño (Oaxacan Chocolate)
recipes.flavorProfile: Grainy, sweet chocolate with toasted almond and cinnamon.
recipes.healthBenefit: Cocoa brings magnesium and iron, and almonds add vitamin E.

ingredients.prepNote: 250 g cacao beans, roasted light brown, skinned and ground

instructions: Grind the cinnamon first.
Grind the roasted cacao with the almonds and cinnamon to a paste.
Add the sugar and grind twice more, then shape into tablets of about 30 g. Each makes one cup whisked into hot milk or water.

nutritionHighlights.note: Sugar is the largest part of each tablet.

citations.source: Ways to Avoid Receta Burnout: Chocolate oaxaqueño

recipes.curationNote: Ways to Avoid Receta Burnout, Chocolate oaxaqueño for every amount and step; made at the source size: 250 g cacao, 500 g sugar, 26 g cinnamon stick, 26 g toasted almonds.

recipes.name: Chicharrón Prensado (Pressed Pork Cracklings in Chile)
recipes.flavorProfile: Rich, chewy pressed pork: shoulder and belly simmered in salted water, then fried golden in their rendered fat and pressed into blocks.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork shoulder and belly bring protein; the belly and its rendered fat make this a rich food.

ingredients.prepNote: 1 teaspoon, stirred into the cooking liquid, which boils off

ingredients.cutPrep: with its skin, cut in 1 cm pieces
ingredients.prepNote: some of its fat drains away as lard when pressed

instructions: Poke holes in the bottoms of a few small containers and make lids that fit inside them. Set them on a rack over a tray lined with paper towels.
Scrape any bristles off the belly skin and cut all the meat into pieces about 1 cm long.
Put the meat in a wide pan. Dissolve the salt in the water and pour it in. Bring to a boil, then cover and cook over medium heat 45 minutes, stirring now and then.
Uncover and keep cooking 15 to 20 minutes, until the water is gone and the fat starts to bubble. Keep stirring until every piece is golden. Watch for spatters.
Lift the pieces into the containers with a slotted spoon, press the lids down hard and weigh them. Let them cool completely; the lard drains into the tray.
Unmould the blocks. They keep about a week in the fridge or a few months frozen.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the pork shoulder and belly.
From the pork belly and the fat it renders.

citations.source: My Slice of Mexico: Homemade pressed pork cracklings

recipes.curationNote: My Slice of Mexico, Homemade pressed pork cracklings (chicharrón prensado casero) for every amount and step; made at the source size, about 3 cups. Salt is the only seasoning; the chile, spices and onion belong to the guisado the pressed meat is later cooked in, not to the chicharrón itself.

recipes.name: Asiento (Unrefined Pork Lard)
recipes.flavorProfile: Toasty, savoury pork fat with browned crackling bits.
recipes.healthBenefit: Almost all fat; spread thin on a tlayuda it carries flavour.

ingredients.prepNote: the fat left at the bottom of the chicharrón pot
the browned bits that settle with it

instructions: When frying chicharrón, pour off the clear fat and keep the cloudy fat and browned bits at the bottom of the pot.
Let it cool and keep it in the fridge up to a month.
One serving is 20 g, spread on a tlayuda or tortilla.

citations.source: Merca MX, Memelas oaxaqueñas de asiento y quesillo

recipes.curationNote: Merca MX, Memelas oaxaqueñas de asiento y quesillo for every amount and step; Describes asiento as the dark lard and browned bits left in the pot after frying chicharrón, with no salt added to it.

recipes.name: Salchichas tipo Viena (Vienna Sausages)
recipes.flavorProfile: Fine, mild, lightly smoked pork and beef sausages.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork and beef bring protein, iron, zinc and B12, with no fillers.

ingredients.prepNote: as crushed ice or ice water
the source uses 18 g salt and 2.5 g Cure #1; nitrite curing salt carries both

ingredients.baseName: Pork, offal and by-products, small intestine
ingredients.prepNote: the source uses sheep casing, 20 to 22 mm; hog intestine stands in
a sausage-making additive no food database lists
ingredients.name: cutter phosphate (sausage binding salt)

instructions: Cut the meat and fat into strips and freeze 1 to 2 hours.
Grind the spices to a fine powder.
Grind the meat and fat twice through a 2 mm plate.
In a food processor, add the salt, spices and phosphate and mix, adding the ice a little at a time, until the mass is smooth and holds together. Keep it at or below 12°C (54°F).
Fill the casings without air pockets and twist into links.
Dry about 1 hour in a smoker, or 10 to 15 minutes at 40°C (104°F) without smoke. Smoke at 60 to 70°C (140 to 158°F) for 45 to 60 minutes.
Poach in 80°C (176°F) water about 15 minutes, then cool in ice water or eat hot.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the curing salt and phosphate.

recipes.curationNote: Wurstcircle, Homemade frankfurter recipe (Vienna sausages) for every amount and step; per 1 kg, the traditional variant: 600 g beef shoulder, 200 g pork shoulder, 200 g back fat.

recipes.name: Jamón Cocido (Cooked Ham)
recipes.flavorProfile: Mild, juicy ham cured in a salt brine with bay, black pepper, garlic and coriander.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork leg is lean, with protein, thiamine, zinc and selenium.

ingredients.cutPrep: boned, skin and outer fat removed
ingredients.prepNote: boneless pork leg, round or top side
the share taken up; the brine holds 30 g
the share taken up; the brine holds 80 g of coarse salt in 1 litre of water

instructions: Dissolve the salt and sugar in the water and add the peppercorns, bay leaves, crushed garlic and coriander. Inject a little brine into the middle of the meat if you have a syringe, for an even cure.
Submerge the meat in the brine and refrigerate 24 to 48 hours.
Lift it out, dry it well and tie it firmly into a cylinder with butcher’s twine, or wrap it tightly in cooking film.
Cook it in water held at about 80°C (176°F), never boiling, about 1 hour per kilo, until the centre reads 68 to 72°C (155 to 162°F).
Plunge it into ice water to stop the cooking, then refrigerate at least 12 hours before slicing.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the salt brine the meat is cured in.

citations.source: Diario UNO: Cómo hacer jamón cocido natural casero

recipes.curationNote: Diario UNO, Cómo hacer jamón cocido natural casero for every amount and step; 1.5 to 2 kg pork leg (bola de lomo or nalga) in a brine of 1 litre water, 80 g coarse salt and 30 g sugar, with black peppercorns, bay, crushed garlic and a pinch of coriander, not measured. No curing salt, so it cooks grey-pink, not pink.

recipes.name: Chiles Chipotles en Adobo
recipes.flavorProfile: Smoky, hot, tangy and a little sweet.
recipes.healthBenefit: Dried chillies and tomato; used a chile at a time.

ingredients.cutPrep: toasted 1 to 2 minutes, soaked 20 to 30 minutes
ingredients.prepNote: 18 to 20 chipotle moritas; dried red chilli stands in for the smoked chile

ingredients.cutPrep: most blended, a little finely diced

ingredients.prepNote: ¾ cup, or the soaking liquid if it does not taste bitter

instructions: Wipe the chiles clean with a damp towel. Toast them in a 400°F (200°C) oven for 1 to 2 minutes, then cover with hot water and soak 20 to 30 minutes. Taste the soaking liquid; if it is bitter, use plain water for the sauce.
Roast the tomato at 400°F (200°C) for 20 to 30 minutes.
Stem and seed 6 or 7 of the chiles and blend them with the tomato, most of the onion, 1 garlic clove, the brown sugar and ½ cup of the water.
Finely dice the rest of the onion and soften it in the oil over medium heat. Add the minced garlic, oregano, cumin, salt and pepper and stir briefly.
Add the purée, vinegar, the last ¼ cup of water and the remaining whole chiles. Simmer 10 to 15 minutes, until reduced. Taste for salt. Keep in a pint jar in the fridge for several weeks.

nutritionHighlights.note: About 80 mg sodium per chile with its sauce.

citations.source: Mexican Please: Homemade chipotles in adobo

recipes.curationNote: Mexican Please, Homemade chipotles in adobo for every amount and step; made at the source size, one pint jar of 18 to 20 moritas. Black pepper and oil are not measured in the source.

recipes.name: Longaniza (Fresh Pork Sausage)
recipes.flavorProfile: Garlicky, tangy and spiced, with chile.
recipes.healthBenefit: Pork protein, with a good deal of fat and salt.

ingredients.cutPrep: stemmed, seeded and boiled until soft
ingredients.prepNote: 8 guajillos and 1 chile de árbol; dried red chilli stands in
the source salts to taste; 20 g is 2% of the meat, the usual sausage measure

ingredients.baseName: Pork, offal and by-products, small intestine
ingredients.cutPrep: natural hog casing, soaked and rinsed

ingredients.prepNote: no database lists plain ground annatto
ingredients.name: achiote (annatto) powder

instructions: Boil the chiles in water until soft, about 10 minutes. Keep some of the cooking water.
Blend the chiles with the allspice, thyme, cumin, cloves, oregano, marjoram, cinnamon, achiote, vinegar and a little of the cooking water to a smooth paste.
Mix the paste, the finely chopped onion and garlic and the salt into the ground pork and fat. Cover and refrigerate 8 to 12 hours.
Stuff into the soaked casing and tie into links. Fry or grill, or crumble out of the casing. It makes about 1.3 kg.

nutritionHighlights.note: From the salt worked into the meat.

citations.source: Grupo Animal: Cómo hacer longaniza en casa

recipes.curationNote: Grupo Animal, Cómo hacer longaniza en casa for every amount and step; per 1 kg of pork at 80/20 lean to fat, which is our 800 g shoulder and 200 g back fat. The source salts to taste with no amount.
